name: High Side
short_blurb: Central plant — chillers, cooling towers, primary distribution, thermal storage and the hydronic backbone that feeds every air-side device.
intro_paragraphs: High side is the central plant — the chillers, cooling towers, pumps, hydronic piping and thermal storage that produce the chilled water and circulate it through the building. It is where most of the energy is consumed, and where most of the lifetime cost is decided.

Air-cooled and water-cooled plants are designed and executed from a few hundred TR up to 16,000+ TR installed (Common Central Secretariat, New Delhi). Plant topology — parallel chillers, primary-secondary distribution, variable-primary, N+1 or 2N — follows the building's reliability target and the operator's standard. The choice is never default.
approach_paragraphs: Chiller selection is driven by the part-load profile, not the design-day peak. Most buildings operate below 60% of peak load for the majority of operating hours, so plants are staged for high IPLV (integrated part-load value) and tuned through the BMS for optimised setpoints once running.

Hydronic networks are sized in AFT Fathom against an instrumented head-loss budget — actual fitting counts, control-valve authority, branch-balancing discipline. Variable-primary flow is the default for new builds; primary-secondary remains where operators standardise on it. Plate heat exchangers interface district cooling, geothermal loops and process-side circuits with full isolation.

systems.name: Air-cooled & water-cooled chillers
systems.description: Centrifugal, screw and scroll chillers selected for design-day capacity and stage-optimised part-load efficiency. Magnetic-bearing oil-free chillers where harmonics or part-load IPLV matter most.

systems.name: Cooling towers
systems.description: Counter-flow and cross-flow towers sized for site footprint and approach temperature. Variable-speed fans, drift eliminators, basin sweepers and concurrent-maintainable cell isolation for redundancy.

systems.name: Primary–secondary distribution
systems.description: Variable-primary or primary-secondary headers with N+1/2N pump banks on VFDs. Branch-valve TAB to ASHRAE/AABC/NEBB protocols. Plate heat exchangers for process or district-cooling interfaces.

systems.name: Thermal energy storage
systems.description: Chilled-water or ice-based storage for peak-shaving, brownout ride-through, and demand-charge optimisation. Tank stratification design and BMS-integrated charge/discharge logic.

systems.name: Geothermal & alternative sources
systems.description: Geothermal water-cooled VRV and ground-loop systems where site geology permits. Delivered at Nalanda University as part of India's first net-zero campus.

systems.name: Plant-room hydronics
systems.description: Headers, manifolds, expansion tanks, air separators, dirt separators, chemical dosing skids and the metering instrumentation that lets the operator see what the plant is doing.

name: Low Side
short_blurb: Air-side equipment — AHUs, FCUs, VRF, terminal units, ducting and the diffusion strategy that delivers conditioned air to the space.
intro_paragraphs: Low side is everything between the chilled-water pipe and the occupant — air handling units, fan coil units, VRF/VRV indoor units, dedicated outdoor air systems, terminal devices, ducting, dampers and diffusers. It is the part of the system the occupant actually experiences.

Low-side work spans the full range — from a single 500 CFM FCU in a hotel room to a 217-AHU plus 130-MAU installation at the SAEL solar-cell facility in Jewar. Every AHU is sized against the room's heat load and ventilation requirement, every duct route is coordinated in the federated BIM model, and every diffuser is selected for throw, drop and noise.
approach_paragraphs: Air-handling units are selected from the heat-load calculation, the supply-air temperature schedule, and the room's acoustic limit. Coil rows, face velocity and bypass factor are picked deliberately — not from a default AHU configurator. DX, chilled-water and dual-coil arrangements coexist on most projects, sized for their loads.

Ducting is routed in Revit (LOD 400) against the structural and architectural envelope, with all clashes resolved before fabrication release. Duct cross-sections balance pressure-drop budget against space constraint. Site installation is leak-tested to SMACNA class A/B/C as the spec demands.

systems.name: Air handling units (AHUs)
systems.description: Floor-mount and ceiling-suspended AHUs with chilled-water or DX coils, single or dual-fan, plug-fan or housed-fan, with full filtration train. In-house AHU manufacturing capability since 2005.

systems.name: Fan coil units (FCUs)
systems.description: Concealed and exposed FCUs for guest rooms, offices, and zone-level conditioning. EC-motor selection where part-load and acoustics matter; standard PSC where simple control is sufficient.

systems.name: VRF / VRV systems
systems.description: Variable refrigerant volume systems for offices, retail and hospitality where chilled-water plant is over-specified. Heat-recovery topologies where simultaneous heating and cooling exists.

systems.name: Dedicated outdoor air systems (DOAS)
systems.description: DOAS / make-up air units sized to ASHRAE 62.1 ventilation rates with energy recovery (sensible or enthalpy) where climate makes the payback work.

systems.name: Ducting & terminal devices
systems.description: Galvanised steel and pre-insulated aluminium ducting, fabricated to SMACNA, leak-tested to class A/B/C. Diffusers, grilles and VAV terminals selected for throw, drop, noise and architectural integration.

systems.name: Fan filter units (FFUs)
systems.description: Ceiling-mounted FFUs for cleanroom and laboratory zones with HEPA H13/H14 terminal filtration. 13,656 FFUs installed on the SAEL Jewar project alone.

name: Comfort Cooling
short_blurb: Offices, hotels, retail, hospitality and residential — conditioning sized to ASHRAE 62.1/90.1 with occupancy-driven controls and BMS tie-in.
intro_paragraphs: Comfort cooling is the discipline of conditioning spaces designed for human occupancy — corporate offices, hotels, retail malls, hospitality and residential. The performance window is set by ASHRAE 55 (thermal comfort), ASHRAE 62.1 (ventilation) and ASHRAE 90.1 (energy). The objective is invisible: occupants notice when the system is wrong, not when it is right.

Comfort cooling has been delivered across the full range — five-star hotels (Westin, Radisson, Marriott, Crowne Plaza, Holiday Inn), corporate towers (Bharti, Vatika, Spaze), mixed-use developments (Ingka/IKEA Centre, Noida), retail malls, and high-end residential (M3M, DLF, Vatika).
approach_paragraphs: Heat loads are calculated room-by-room against occupancy schedules, fabric U-values, solar gains by orientation and time-of-day, and equipment dissipation. ASHRAE 62.1 ventilation rates are added with simultaneity factors and demand-controlled ventilation where occupancy is dynamic.

Distribution strategies are picked against the building shape and the operator's preference — CHW + AHU/FCU for large commercial; VRF heat-recovery for mid-market offices; DX split for distributed retail. Comfort is verified by an instrumented post-occupancy walk-through, not a tick-box at handover.

systems.name: Office & corporate cooling
systems.description: Floor-by-floor AHUs with VAV terminals, perimeter induction or chilled beams in premium fit-outs. Demand-controlled ventilation tied to CO₂ sensing in conference rooms.

systems.name: Hotel & hospitality cooling
systems.description: Four-pipe FCU systems for guest-room conditioning with simultaneous heating/cooling capability. DOAS for ventilation make-up. Specialist treatment for ballrooms, kitchens and spa zones.

systems.name: Retail & mall cooling
systems.description: Large AHUs with high-induction diffusion for atria and shop-front spaces. Energy recovery on outdoor air. Zoning per tenant package with sub-metering for cost allocation.

systems.name: Residential cooling
systems.description: VRF heat-recovery, split DX or low-static FCUs for premium residential. Acoustic-led selection: NC 25-30 indoor unit specifications in bedrooms.

name: Industrial Cooling
short_blurb: Factory floors, manufacturing halls and warehouses — high-volume air distribution, process-exhaust make-up and equipment cooling at industrial scale.
intro_paragraphs: Industrial cooling serves the manufacturing floor — large open volumes, high equipment dissipation, process exhausts that pull large quantities of make-up air, and operators who need stable conditions for the product, not just for themselves. The discipline blurs into process cooling at one end and comfort cooling at the other.

Industrial HVAC has been delivered for JSW EV manufacturing (Bangalore), Coca-Cola plants, Unilever, BMW, Hyundai, ITC and the IKEA Noida mixed-use development. Scope ranges from large AHU farms feeding factory halls to spot cooling and high-velocity destratification on shed-roof floors.
approach_paragraphs: Heat loads include process equipment dissipation, internal occupancy, solar gain through skylights, infiltration and exhaust make-up. Make-up air for process exhaust is sized to maintain a defined building pressure relative to outside — typically slightly positive to keep dust out, slightly negative where contaminants need containment.

Air distribution favours high-volume, lower-pressure systems with destratification where shed-roof heights cause vertical temperature gradients. Spot cooling for operator stations is treated as a separate scope where the process generates intense local heat.

systems.name: Factory hall AHUs & MAUs
systems.description: Large AHUs and make-up air units sized for the hall's exhaust requirement and operator comfort window. Energy recovery on outdoor air where climate makes the payback work.

systems.name: Process exhaust make-up
systems.description: Make-up air systems sized to maintain the building's pressure regime relative to outside. Heat-recovery wheels on hot-process exhausts where energy density justifies it.

systems.name: Spot & equipment cooling
systems.description: Localised cooling for high-dissipation equipment — battery-line cells, welding stations, paint booths, CNC enclosures. Treated separately from the hall's general comfort cooling.

systems.name: Destratification & high-velocity distribution
systems.description: HVLS (high-volume low-speed) fans for shed-roof destratification. High-velocity diffusion in tall halls where conventional throw is insufficient.

name: Data Center Cooling
short_blurb: White-space conditioning for colocation, hyperscale and HPC — aisle containment, CRAH/InRow/RDHX, liquid-ready paths and Tier 3/4-ready resilience.
intro_paragraphs: Data centre cooling is a discipline of its own. The load is dense, the resilience target is uncompromising, the supply-air window is narrow, and the operator's commissioning protocol is exact. MEPF has been delivered for data centres including STT GDC (Mumbai), CtrlS (Navi Mumbai), Digital Edge (BOM01), Anant Raj Cloud and STPI.

Every white-space layout is built around supply-air temperature management to ASHRAE TC 9.9, contained aisles, redundant cooling distribution, and a clear migration path to liquid for AI/HPC density. The cooling plant — chillers, towers, hydronics — is engineered for concurrent maintainability, with all faults discovered in commissioning rather than during the operator's first failover drill.
approach_paragraphs: Air-side strategy is settled at design — hot/cold-aisle containment, perimeter CRAH or InRow units for medium-density halls, rear-door heat exchangers for high-density rows, liquid manifolds reserved at the cabinet for future HPC build-out. Supply-air setpoints are tuned to ASHRAE TC 9.9 with the operator's risk tolerance.

PUE is treated as a design output, not a marketing number. Free-cooling hours are calculated against the site's wet-bulb profile (water-side economiser) or dry-bulb (air-side where envelope permits). Chiller staging, pump VFDs and tower fan VFDs are sequenced for low part-load energy.

systems.name: Aisle containment & airflow strategy
systems.description: Hot-aisle or cold-aisle containment with brush seals at row ends, blanking panels in unused U-positions, and BMS-monitored supply-air temperature across the cold aisle. Supply-air managed to ASHRAE TC 9.9.

systems.name: CRAH / CRAC perimeter cooling
systems.description: Perimeter chilled-water CRAH units with EC plug fans, variable supply-air capacity, and BMS-modulated chilled-water valves. DX-based CRAC for sites without central chilled-water plant.

systems.name: InRow & rear-door heat exchangers
systems.description: InRow cooling units placed within the cabinet row for medium-high density loads. Rear-door heat exchangers for high-density (15-30 kW/rack) zones, including AI and HPC build-outs.

systems.name: Liquid-ready architecture
systems.description: Reserved liquid manifolds and cabinet-level Coolant Distribution Unit (CDU) drops for AI/HPC build-out. Direct-Liquid-Cooling pre-stubbed taps designed for non-disruptive migration from air to liquid.

systems.name: Chilled-water plant & hydronics
systems.description: Air- or water-cooled chillers sized for design-day ambient, staged for part-load efficiency. Primary–secondary or variable-primary headers with N+1/2N pumps on VFDs. Concurrent-maintainable cell isolation on towers.

systems.name: Leak detection & containment
systems.description: Zoned water-leak detection (WLD) under raised floors and along piping runs. BMS-integrated alarm hierarchy. Isolation valves at fault zones. Drip pans and bunding around all wet equipment.

name: Process Cooling
short_blurb: Cleanroom HVAC (ISO 6/7/8), process cooling water, pressure cascade and HEPA-filtered air for semiconductor, pharma and laboratory environments.
intro_paragraphs: Process cooling is the most exacting discipline in the HVAC stack. The performance window is set by the process — ISO 14644-1 cleanroom class, pressure cascade between zones, supply-air ACPH, temperature and humidity tolerance — and the system is engineered against the tighter of the tender spec and the governing standard.

Class 10,000 / 100,000 (ISO 7/8) cleanrooms have been executed at scale for Foxconn (Apple) in Bangalore — wall and ceiling PUF panelling, epoxy flooring, HEPA-filtered AHUs, return-air risers, cleanroom doors and view panels — and the SAEL Jewar 5.75 GW solar-cell facility, with ISO 6/7/8 zones across 66,000+ sqm, 13,656 FFUs, 217 AHUs and 130 MAUs.
approach_paragraphs: Cleanroom design follows a deliberate workflow: concept zoning by ISO class and pressure strategy; room-by-room heat-load with tool dissipation per OEM datasheet; FFU and HEPA banding; pressure cascade with door-interlock logic; federated BIM at LOD 400 with all clashes resolved before shop release. Validation tests particle count, recovery time, ACPH, ΔP, T/RH, noise and lighting against ISO 14644-3 test methods.

Process cooling water (PCW) is a separate, closed-loop system with SS 316 / PP-H piping, hydro and pneumatic testing, conductivity and leak taps, and OEM-validated hookups. Primary-secondary distribution with plate heat exchangers isolates the process loop from the building's chilled-water plant. Delivered for Foxconn India and the JSW EV battery-line cleanroom.

systems.name: Cleanroom HVAC (ISO 6/7/8)
systems.description: HEPA-filtered AHUs with laminar-airflow ducting, pressure cascade between zones (≥15 Pa typical for ISO 6), tight T/RH stability (±1 °C, ±5% RH), HEPA H13/H14 gel-seal terminal filtration with in-situ leak testing.

systems.name: Fan filter units (FFUs)
systems.description: Ceiling-grid FFUs for unidirectional or semi-directional flow in ISO 6/7 zones. Low-turbulence supply with terminal HEPA H13/H14 gel-seal filtration. 13,656 FFUs installed at SAEL alone.

systems.name: Process cooling water (PCW)
systems.description: Closed-loop process-water headers with SS 316 / PP-H piping, primary-secondary interfaces, plate heat exchanger to building CHW. Conductivity and leak taps. OEM-validated hookups. Hydro + pneumatic testing.

systems.name: Pressure cascade & airflow strategy
systems.description: Deliberate pressure cascade between zones with door-interlock logic, emergency purge paths, and cross-contamination modelling. Controlled return-air architecture with low-level returns for particle sweep-out.

systems.name: CDA, nitrogen & vacuum
systems.description: Compressed dry air, nitrogen and vacuum distribution networks routed with strict slope control, leak-tested to stringent standards, integrated without compromising the contamination zone. Delivered for Foxconn cleanroom and Tata Dholera utility piping.

systems.name: Pharma & lab process cooling
systems.description: USP / EP-grade water systems, controlled-temperature process loops, dehumidification and reheat for tight RH-tolerant manufacturing — cosmetics, pharmaceutical, lens and animal-biotech facilities, including NIAB Hyderabad.

name: Foundations & Structural
short_blurb: Raft, pile and combined foundations engineered against soil investigation, load take-down and seismic zone.
intro_paragraphs: Every foundation begins with a geotechnical report and ends with an instrumented pour. In between, the structural team models the superstructure load take-down, sizes the reinforcement cage, and coordinates the pour with MEP cast-in openings so penetrations are not cut retrospectively.

Pile caps and rafts are delivered with continuous third-party inspection — cube tests at prescribed ages, rebound hammer and ultrasonic readings on key pours, and crack-monitoring protocols during backfill. Deep excavations are shored with design-specific retention systems rather than generic steel sheet piles.
approach_paragraphs: Design follows IS 456, IS 875 and IS 1893 with seismic zone-specific detailing. Reinforcement bar-bending schedules are model-derived and reconciled with the architectural and MEP federated model before fabrication, eliminating field surprises.

Pours are pre-mobilised with batching schedule, transit-mixer routing and pump positioning agreed against the structural inspection plan. Concrete cubes are sampled at agreed intervals and tested by NABL-accredited labs.

systems.name: Pile foundations
systems.description: Driven, bored and cast-in-situ piles sized to soil bearing capacity and load take-down. Pile integrity tests on every pour.

systems.name: Raft & combined footings
systems.description: Mat foundations for high column-load buildings and combined footings for asymmetric load patterns. Cast in instrumented continuous strips.

systems.name: Substructure & retaining
systems.description: Basement walls, retaining structures and shoring for deep excavations. Water-stop detailing at construction joints; sealed against groundwater intrusion.

name: Façades & Envelope
short_blurb: Unitised and stick-system curtain walls, ACP cladding and structural glazing sealed against the building envelope.
intro_paragraphs: Façades are engineered for wind load, seismic drift, thermal movement and water tightness — in that order. The façade desk works from the architect's elevation, runs a wind-tunnel-backed pressure grid, and sizes the mullion-transom rhythm accordingly.

Every panel is factory-glazed where possible. Site joints are backer-rod-and-sealant details, water-tested in mock-up before mass production, and inspected in lift-by-lift hose-test batches. Anchorage is to a shear-connector bracket — never direct to the slab edge.
approach_paragraphs: Performance is verified on a full-scale mock-up before mass production: AAMA 501 water penetration, AAMA 502 field hose test, and structural deflection per ASCE 7. Thermal performance is measured to ISO 12567.
Anchorage drawings are stamped by the structural team and verified against the as-built slab edge — corrections are detailed at the bracket, never at the panel.

systems.name: Unitised curtain walls
systems.description: Factory-glazed, factory-sealed panels lifted to the slab edge as complete units. Faster install, tighter quality, fewer site joints.

systems.name: Stick-system glazing
systems.description: Site-assembled mullion-and-transom systems for buildings with complex geometry or constrained access where unitised lifts aren't feasible.

systems.name: ACP & metal cladding
systems.description: Aluminium composite panels, zinc and copper rainscreen systems on through-fastened or hidden-fixing rails. Fire-rated cores per local code.

name: Industrial Flooring
short_blurb: Trimix, vacuum-dewatered and epoxy-resin floors designed for point loads, abrasion and chemical exposure.
intro_paragraphs: An industrial floor is a structural element, not a finish. Floor specification picks slab thickness, joint spacing, reinforcement type and surface treatment against the expected wheel load, turning radius and chemical contact — not off a generic manufacturer cut-sheet.

Pours are laser-screeded in continuous strips to minimise cold joints. Surface hardeners are broadcast wet-on-wet; post-cure, joints are saw-cut on schedule and filled with semi-rigid joint filler so pallet trucks do not spall the arrises.
approach_paragraphs: Slab design follows TR 34 (UK) or ACI 360 (US) — pick depends on the operator. Reinforcement is typically steel fibre + post-tension where joint count must be minimised; conventional rebar where simpler logistics matter more.
Flatness is verified on the day of pour to FF/FL Class per ASTM E1155. Defects identified in the verification walk are diamond-ground before handover, not painted over.

systems.name: Power-floated concrete
systems.description: Trimix and vacuum-dewatered concrete floors with broadcast surface hardeners. The volume workhorse for warehouses and factory halls.

systems.name: Epoxy & PU resin floors
systems.description: Self-levelling epoxy and polyurethane systems for cleanroom, pharma, food processing and laboratory environments.

systems.name: Joint-free pours
systems.description: Post-tension and steel-fibre floors that minimise joint count for high-MHE-traffic facilities — fewer joints means fewer maintenance failures.

name: Corporate Interiors
short_blurb: Tenant fit-out delivered to the developer's warm-shell handover — ceilings, partitions, joinery, flooring and finishes.
intro_paragraphs: Corporate interiors sit at the intersection of three trades — ceiling and partition systems, MEP services feeding them, and the bespoke joinery that reads as the client's brand. All three are detailed against a single reflected ceiling plan so grid, diffuser and light fitting lines agree.

Finishes are sample-approved before production, mocked up on a pilot bay, and sealed against the as-built drawing. Snag-list resolution is tracked on a floor-by-floor register and signed off before the client commissioning walk.
approach_paragraphs: The team works from a coordinated reflected ceiling plan that resolves MEP, lighting, ceiling grid and sprinkler heads in a single drawing. Acoustic and FF&E specs are signed off against the project brief at scheme stage, not retrofit-corrected at handover.
Joinery is shop-fabricated against approved samples; site installation is dry-fit before final fix to identify dimensional creep early.

systems.name: Ceiling & partition systems
systems.description: T-bar, gypsum, plank-ceilings and metal-pan systems with integrated MEP coordination. Demountable partitions where workplace flexibility matters.

systems.name: Joinery & FF&E
systems.description: Bespoke reception desks, pantry counters, meeting-room storage and acoustic feature walls fabricated in-house and finished to sample approval.

systems.name: Flooring & finishes
systems.description: Carpet tile, vinyl plank, engineered timber and stone finishes selected for acoustic, slip-resistance and maintenance profile.

name: Retrofitting & Strengthening
short_blurb: Structural strengthening, façade replacement and MEP modernisation for ageing or repurposed building stock.
intro_paragraphs: Retrofitting is the discipline of rebuilding without demolishing — strengthening a structure, replacing a façade, upgrading MEP services in a building that must remain partially or fully operational. The constraints are tighter than new-build: load paths must transition smoothly, occupants must be protected, and the historical record of the asset becomes the design baseline.

Retrofit work has been delivered for IT-park BMS upgrades, healthcare facility expansions, and façade replacements on operating commercial buildings. Each engagement begins with a forensic survey and an MEP system condition audit.
approach_paragraphs: Forensic surveys use non-destructive testing — rebound hammer, ultrasonic pulse velocity, half-cell potential — to map structural condition before strengthening. Designs use carbon-fibre wrap, jacketing or steel collars depending on the load case.
Operational continuity is engineered into the works programme. Floor-by-floor or shift-based phasing keeps the asset producing revenue while the upgrade proceeds.

systems.name: Structural strengthening
systems.description: Carbon-fibre wrap, RCC jacketing, steel collars and base-isolation retrofits for buildings requiring increased load capacity or seismic upgrade.

systems.name: Façade replacement
systems.description: Replacing curtain-wall or cladding systems while the building remains occupied. Phased lift-by-lift removal and re-glazing with weather-protection screens.

systems.name: MEP modernisation
systems.description: BMS upgrade, chiller-plant replacement, lighting retrofit and fire-system upgrade for operating buildings — designed for minimum disruption.

name: HT & LT Distribution
short_blurb: High-tension to low-tension distribution — 33/22/11 kV systems, transformers, LV switchgear and the cable management that ties them.
intro_paragraphs: Electrical distribution is engineered, not assembled. Single-line diagrams, short-circuit analysis, protection coordination and arc-flash modelling are run end-to-end before the first cable is pulled. Cable trays and bus trunking are routed in the coordinated MEPF model so service voids stay congestion-free.

HT/LT scope spans the full voltage hierarchy — from 33 kV HV reception through transformers, LV switchgear, busbar trunking, and feeder cabling to the final distribution panel. The same team that engineers it tests and commissions it.
approach_paragraphs: Short-circuit analysis and protection coordination are run in ETAP or DigSILENT against the operator's grid impedance. Relay settings are commissioned via primary injection — never by setting the dial blind.
Cable routes are coordinated in Revit with all other MEPF services and structural openings. Cable trays are sized for 30% future-load growth as a baseline.

systems.name: HT reception & ring main
systems.description: 33 / 22 / 11 kV HT systems with ring-main units, vacuum circuit breakers, and SCADA-integrated metering at the point of reception.

systems.name: LV switchgear & MCC
systems.description: Form-2b/3b/4 LV switchgear, motor control centres, intelligent breakers with networked trip units, and BMS-integrated metering.

systems.name: Cable distribution
systems.description: MV/LV cable distribution on cable trays, ladders and direct burial. Fire-resistant cable for life-safety circuits; XLPE for the rest.

name: Substations & Transformers
short_blurb: Indoor and outdoor substations, dry-type and oil-immersed transformers, sized to the load profile and the operator's reliability target.
intro_paragraphs: Substations are where the building meets the grid. The scope covers indoor and outdoor substations, package substations, transformer foundations, oil containment pits, and the protection coordination that integrates them with both upstream utility and downstream load.

Transformer selection is driven by load profile, harmonic distortion, ambient temperature and the operator's preference for dry-type vs oil-immersed — never defaulted; every project gets its own thermal and harmonic analysis.
approach_paragraphs: Transformer sizing considers the actual load profile, not just nameplate kVA. Harmonic content is modelled where IT, VFD or LED loads dominate; K-factor or harmonic mitigation specified accordingly.
Oil containment is sized for full transformer oil volume + 10%, with hydrocarbon-trap drainage. Outdoor substations are detailed for monsoon ingress and rodent protection.

systems.name: Indoor & outdoor substations
systems.description: Compact indoor substations for urban sites, outdoor package substations for industrial campuses, with full protection and metering integration.

systems.name: Dry-type transformers
systems.description: Cast-resin and VPI dry-type transformers for indoor applications, IT loads, and where fire/oil-containment risk must be avoided.

systems.name: Oil-immersed transformers
systems.description: ONAN/ONAF transformers for outdoor installations, with oil containment, Buchholz protection, and BMS-integrated temperature monitoring.

name: Backup Power (DG & UPS)
short_blurb: Diesel generation, static UPS and battery rooms for ride-through, brownout protection and tier-3/4 data-centre uptime.
intro_paragraphs: Backup power keeps the building producing when the grid stops. Diesel generation is delivered sized for full IT + cooling block load, day tanks and bulk fuel skids, modular static UPS systems with ventilated battery rooms, and the protection logic that orchestrates failover automatically.

For data centres and semiconductor fabs, the topology is concurrent-maintainable or fault-tolerant — designed against the Uptime Institute Tier rating the operator targets, and commissioned with load-bank testing to prove it.
approach_paragraphs: DG sizing accounts for motor inrush (typically 6× FLA for non-soft-started loads), step-loading sequence, and harmonic content from VFDs and rectifiers. Load step verification is part of commissioning, not assumed at design.

UPS battery rooms are ventilated to limit hydrogen accumulation per IEEE 1187 — with BMS-integrated H₂ sensing on every site. Failover paths are designed concurrent-maintainable where the Tier requires it.

systems.name: Diesel generation
systems.description: DG sets sized for full IT + cooling block load, with day tanks, bulk fuel storage, UL-certified fuel transfer and polishing skids, and explosion-proof control stations.

systems.name: Modular UPS
systems.description: Static modular UPS topologies sized for IT load with N+1 or 2N redundancy. VRLA or Li-ion battery rooms with BMS-integrated monitoring.

systems.name: ATS & synchronisation
systems.description: Automatic transfer switches with break-before-make or closed-transition logic. DG paralleling with active power management for multi-set installations.

name: Bus Trunking & Switchgear
short_blurb: Sandwich-construction busbar trunking, panel manufacturing and the LV distribution that powers every downstream load.
intro_paragraphs: Busbar trunking is the workhorse of high-rise and high-density power distribution. Sandwich-construction BBT delivers higher fault current rating, lower impedance, and faster reconfiguration than equivalent cable runs. The scope covers the BBT itself and the LV distribution panels it feeds.

Panels are built to Form 2b/3b/4 segregation per IEC 61439, with ICW ratings sized to the upstream fault level. Every panel is type-tested or design-verified — never assembled to a generic single-line without engineering review.
approach_paragraphs: BBT routing is coordinated with structural slab openings and service voids during BIM coordination, not site-adapted. Fire-rated penetrations use UL-certified sleeves and intumescent collars.

Panel manufacturing uses Schneider, ABB, Siemens or L&T component sets per the operator's standard. ICW ratings are coordinated with the upstream fault level and breaker selectivity verified by analysis.

systems.name: Sandwich BBT
systems.description: High-fault-rating sandwich busbar trunking for risers and horizontal runs. Modular tap-off boxes for flexibility in fit-out and future loads.

systems.name: LV distribution panels
systems.description: Main LT panels, sub-distribution boards, motor control centres — built to Form 2b/3b/4 segregation, type-tested or design-verified.

systems.name: Final distribution
systems.description: Sub-panels, distribution boards and final-circuit MCBs. Selectivity coordination so faults clear at the closest upstream device, not the main breaker.

name: Critical & Cleanroom Lighting
short_blurb: Cleanroom-rated LED, emergency egress, life-safety lighting and DALI / KNX-controlled architectural systems.
intro_paragraphs: Lighting in critical environments is more than illumination. Cleanroom luminaires must be flush-glazed, sealed against contamination, and rated for in-situ HEPA leak testing. Emergency lighting must hold the egress lumens through a defined battery duration. Architectural lighting must be DALI-addressable and tunable.
Lighting scope spans cleanroom-rated LED arrays, life-safety emergency systems, architectural DALI/KNX controls, and the photometric design that ties them to the room's task and acoustic budget.
approach_paragraphs: Photometric design is run in DIALux or AGi32 against the room's task plane illuminance target. Glare is verified by UGR calculation; acoustic impact by NC rating. Cleanroom luminaires are selected for HEPA-compatibility and IP rating per the zone class.

Emergency egress lighting is sized for 1.0 lux average on the centre-line of egress paths with 90-minute battery duration. Test logic is monthly self-test, annual discharge, BMS-monitored where present.

systems.name: Cleanroom LED
systems.description: Sealed cleanroom-rated LED arrays compatible with HEPA grid layouts. IP65+ rating, gasket-sealed housings, and zero air infiltration through fitting.

systems.name: Emergency & egress lighting
systems.description: Self-contained and centrally-monitored emergency luminaires with 90-minute battery duration. BMS-tied test reporting where present.

systems.name: Architectural & DALI control
systems.description: DALI / KNX-addressable luminaires with scene control, daylight harvesting, occupancy sensing and BMS integration for energy management.

name: EPMS — Electrical Power Monitoring
short_blurb: Electrical Power Monitoring Systems across HV/LV/UPS/DG with per-rack PDU telemetry and arc-flash event capture.
intro_paragraphs: EPMS is the metering and monitoring layer that tells the operator what their electrical system is actually doing. Per-feeder, per-panel and per-rack metering is delivered, integrated into a unified historian — so power quality, energy consumption and event capture are observable in real time.
For data centres and tier-1 industrial facilities, EPMS feeds both the BMS and the operator's DCIM. Open feeds (Modbus, BACnet, SNMP) ensure the data is portable, not vendor-locked.
approach_paragraphs: Metering granularity follows the operator's billing, allocation or analytics need — feeder-level for buildings, branch-circuit for premium colocation, per-rack PDU for high-density IT.
Power quality monitoring captures harmonics, voltage sag/swell and arc-flash events. Trend logging into a historian with 1-second resolution where the operator's PQ window demands it.

systems.name: Feeder & branch metering
systems.description: Class-1 energy meters at every panel feeder, with branch-circuit monitoring where allocation matters. Communications via Modbus RTU/TCP or BACnet.

systems.name: Power quality monitoring
systems.description: PQ analyzers at the LV main and critical feeders capturing harmonics, sag/swell, transients and flicker. EN 50160 compliant reporting.

systems.name: Per-rack PDU & DCIM tie-in
systems.description: Intelligent rack PDUs with per-outlet metering, environmental sensing, and SNMP/Modbus feeds into the operator's DCIM.

name: Water Treatment (WTP/STP/ETP)
short_blurb: Water treatment plants, sewage treatment plants and effluent treatment plants sized to source-water analysis and discharge consent.
intro_paragraphs: Water treatment plants are sized against the source-water analysis, consumer demand, and discharge consent — not as a generic 'WTP block' on the BOQ. Membrane systems, multi-grade filters, softeners and dosing skids are specified to a clear treatment objective.

The scope covers raw-water treatment for cooling-tower make-up and process water, sewage treatment for building blackwater, and effluent treatment for industrial process discharge. Sludge management and dewatering close the loop.
approach_paragraphs: Source-water analysis is the starting point — TDS, hardness, iron, silica, coliforms — and the treatment train is built to remove what's actually present. Membrane configuration (RO + NF + UF) is sized to the recovery target.

Sewage and effluent treatment use MBBR, SBR or membrane bioreactor processes depending on footprint, BOD/COD load, and discharge requirement. Online instrumentation (pH, ORP, turbidity) feeds the BMS for trend logging and alarms.

systems.name: Water treatment plant (WTP)
systems.description: RO-based and conventional WTPs for cooling-tower make-up, process water and potable water. Multi-grade + activated carbon + softener pre-treatment as required.

systems.name: Sewage treatment plant (STP)
systems.description: MBBR / SBR / MBR plants for building blackwater. Treated water reused for flushing and landscape irrigation per IGBC/LEED guidelines.

systems.name: Effluent treatment plant (ETP)
systems.description: Industrial effluent treatment sized to the operator's BOD/COD load. Physical-chemical pre-treatment + biological + tertiary polishing for ZLD where required.

name: Industrial Piping
short_blurb: High-purity SS 316 / PP-H piping for semiconductor, pharma and laboratory process water, conductivity-monitored end-to-end.
intro_paragraphs: Industrial piping is the discipline that delivers fluids — water, chemicals, gases, steam — through a building's process layer. Pipe material, jointing method, slope and supports are picked against the fluid, the pressure, the temperature and the cleanliness requirement of the downstream load.

SS 316 PCW networks have been delivered for Foxconn cleanroom, JSW EV battery-line cooling, and SAEL solar-cell process loops. Every joint is welded, leak-tested, and conductivity-tapped for monitoring.
approach_paragraphs: Pipe routing is coordinated in Revit (LOD 400) with all other MEPF services. Slope and support intervals follow ASME B31.3 for process piping; isometric drawings are signed off pre-fabrication.

Welding is qualified to ASME IX with continuous third-party inspection on critical SS 316 and PP-H joints. Hydrostatic and pneumatic tests are witnessed by the operator; conductivity taps allow real-time leak monitoring in production.

systems.name: Process cooling water (PCW)
systems.description: Closed-loop SS 316 / PP-H PCW networks with primary-secondary distribution, plate heat exchanger isolation, hydro + pneumatic testing, conductivity monitoring.

systems.name: Compressed Dry Air (CDA)
systems.description: Oil-free compressor + dryer skids feeding multi-stage filtration to dew-point and particulate class. SS and aluminium distribution with POU regulators.

systems.name: Specialty gases (N₂ · Vacuum)
systems.description: Nitrogen, vacuum and process-gas distribution with strict slope control, leak testing, OEM-validated POU hookups. Delivered at Foxconn and Tata Dholera.

name: Hydropneumatic Systems
short_blurb: Variable-frequency pump banks with pressure-vessel control for constant-pressure water supply across high-rise and large-format buildings.
intro_paragraphs: Hydropneumatic systems deliver constant water pressure across multi-level buildings without overhead tanks on every zone. VFD-controlled pump banks ride a pressure vessel buffer, maintaining setpoint pressure regardless of demand.

Designs use duty-standby logic with sequencing for high-demand events, pressure-reducing zones for low-floor pressure management, and BMS integration so the building operator can see pump-run hours, suction pressure and fault status in real time.
approach_paragraphs: Pump sizing follows the calculated peak simultaneous demand with simultaneity factors per IS 1172. VFD curves are tuned during commissioning to the actual building hydraulics, not the catalogue duty point.
Pressure-reducing valves protect lower-floor fixtures from over-pressure; air-relief valves at high points prevent waterhammer. The whole system is BMS-monitored with trended pressure profiles.

systems.name: VFD pump banks
systems.description: Duty-standby or N+1 VFD pump banks with pressure-vessel buffer and PLC-driven sequencing logic. Soft-start and ramp-down to eliminate waterhammer.

systems.name: Pressure management
systems.description: Zoned PRVs to manage pressure across building stack. Air-relief valves at high points. Pipe network sized to AFT Fathom hydraulic model.

systems.name: Hot water systems
systems.description: Heat-pump or boiler-fed hot water with circulation loops, thermostatic mixing valves and Legionella-compliant temperature control.

name: Sanitary & Plumbing
short_blurb: Soil, waste, vent and water-supply piping with fixture-grade finishes for corporate, hospitality, healthcare and residential buildings.
intro_paragraphs: Sanitary plumbing covers the building's water-supply and drainage layers — cold and hot water distribution, soil and waste stacks, vent piping and the fixture-grade finishes the occupant sees. The discipline rewards quiet execution: occupants notice when it's wrong, not when it's right.

Systems are delivered to IPC, ISPC and CPHEEO standards, with traps and venting sized per stack height. Pipe materials are CPVC for water supply, PVC-DWV or HDPE for drainage, with fixture-grade sanitaryware per the operator's spec (Kohler, TOTO, Roca, Grohe).
approach_paragraphs: Hydraulic design follows fixture-unit calculation per IPC/ISPC. Stack venting is sized to prevent siphonage and back-pressure across the full stack height. Drainage gradients are verified on-site, not assumed.
Sanitaryware is installed against architect-approved templates with finish-level integration to floor and wall tile lines. Joinery and counter mountings are coordinated with the interior fit-out.

systems.name: Water supply
systems.description: CPVC or PEX water-supply piping for cold and hot lines. Sized to fixture-unit demand with simultaneity factors. Isolation at every wet wall.

systems.name: Soil, waste & vent
systems.description: PVC-DWV or HDPE stacks with full vent system per IPC/ISPC. Cleanouts at every change of direction; floor traps with primer connections.

systems.name: Fixtures & sanitaryware
systems.description: Architect-approved fixture installations from premium OEMs. Concealed flush plates and wall-hung WCs supported on Geberit-class frames.

name: Steam Boilers
short_blurb: Process steam generation, distribution and condensate recovery for hospitality, pharma, laundry and process-load applications.
intro_paragraphs: Steam is the working fluid for laundry, kitchen, sterilisation and many pharma process loads. The scope covers oil-fired, gas-fired and electric boilers, steam distribution piping, pressure-reducing stations and condensate recovery — sized to the operator's peak and average load.

Distribution is to ASME B31.1 with insulated, traced piping where heat loss matters. Condensate return reduces fresh-water make-up and recovers thermal energy; condensate-quality monitoring protects the boiler from contamination.
approach_paragraphs: Boiler sizing accounts for peak instantaneous demand with diversity, not just averaged daily load. Combustion efficiency is tuned at commissioning and verified annually with stack-O₂ measurement.

Condensate recovery is engineered with deaerator, feed pumps and conductivity-controlled blowdown. Steam traps are surveyed annually — leaking traps are the largest source of steam-system energy loss.

systems.name: Steam generation
systems.description: Fire-tube and water-tube boilers, oil-fired, gas-fired or electric per fuel availability. Modular installations for redundancy and turn-down.

systems.name: Steam distribution
systems.description: Insulated steam mains with drip-leg drainage, pressure-reducing stations at usage points, and full ASME B31.1 compliance.

systems.name: Condensate recovery
systems.description: Deaerator + feed-pump skids returning condensate to the boiler. Conductivity-controlled blowdown protects boiler from contamination.

name: Rainwater Harvesting
short_blurb: Rooftop collection, storage and ground-water recharge systems compliant with IGBC, LEED and CGWB groundwater regulations.
intro_paragraphs: Rainwater harvesting captures and either stores or recharges runoff from rooftop and paved-area collection. Storage systems use the water for landscape irrigation or non-potable supply; recharge systems return it to the aquifer through borewell or pit infiltration.
Designs follow CGWB guidelines and local municipal requirements, with first-flush diversion, sand-and-charcoal filtration, and overflow management for high-intensity rainfall events.
approach_paragraphs: Collection area is calculated against catchment runoff coefficient and design storm intensity. Storage volume is sized for the operator's intended use; recharge pits are sized to local soil percolation rate.
First-flush diverters protect storage from the dirty initial runoff. Filtration is sized to maintain water quality for the intended end-use — finer for non-potable supply, coarser for landscape only.

systems.name: Rooftop collection
systems.description: Roof drains, gutters, downcomers and collection chambers with first-flush diversion. Routed to storage tank or recharge pit per design.

systems.name: Storage & reuse
systems.description: Polyethylene or RCC storage tanks with filtration train (sand + carbon + UV) for non-potable reuse — flushing, landscape, cooling-tower make-up.

systems.name: Groundwater recharge
systems.description: Recharge pits and borewell injection systems returning surplus runoff to the aquifer. Sized to local soil percolation and depth-to-water.

name: Fire Hydrant Systems
short_blurb: Wet and dry riser hydrant systems with electric, diesel and jockey pump sets to NBC 2016 and IS 13039.
intro_paragraphs: Fire hydrants are the building's first-response wet supply. Yard hydrants for external attack, wet-riser hydrants for internal attack from staircase landings — each sized for the building's classification, height and floor area per NBC 2016.

Pump-set design is electric main + diesel standby + jockey, with auto-changeover sequenced for grid failure. Static and pumping pressure are hydraulically modelled to verify pressure and flow at the most-remote hydrant.
approach_paragraphs: Static tank sizing follows NBC 2016 for the building's occupancy class. Pump curves are selected against the calculated most-remote hydrant flow and pressure — not over-sized to a default.
Commissioning runs full flow tests with the local fire authority witness. NOC and Form A are obtained before handover, not as an afterthought.

systems.name: Hydrant network
systems.description: Yard and landing hydrants on MS or galvanised piping with isolation valves at every branch. Hose cabinets stocked per IS 884.

systems.name: Pump house
systems.description: Electric main + diesel standby + jockey pump set with auto-changeover and remote alarm to BMS. Suction from underground or overhead static tank.

systems.name: Static water storage
systems.description: Underground or overhead static tank sized per NBC 2016 for the building's occupancy. Make-up from municipal or borewell with float valves.

name: Sprinkler Systems
short_blurb: Wet-pipe, dry-pipe and pre-action sprinkler systems designed to NFPA 13 hydraulic calculation for the building's hazard class.
intro_paragraphs: Sprinkler systems are designed to NFPA 13 with explicit hydraulic calculation — density, area of operation, K-factor, most-remote-head pressure all locked at design freeze. Generic schematic systems get rejected at the fire-authority NOC stage — properly engineered ones don't.

Wet-pipe is the volume workhorse. Dry-pipe goes into unheated zones (loading docks, garages). Pre-action systems with UL/FM-listed valves go into data halls and museum stores where false-trip prevention matters.
approach_paragraphs: Hydraulic calculations are performed in HASS, Elite or Sprink-CALC against the building's hazard class (Light, OH-1 to OH-3, EH). K-factor and density are picked deliberately — not defaulted.

On data-centre projects, pre-action systems use cross-zoned detection (smoke + heat) for release, with electric supervisory air on the dry-pilot line. Discharge testing is performed during commissioning.

systems.name: Wet-pipe sprinklers
systems.description: Standard wet-pipe systems for heated, fully-occupied spaces. K-factor and density per hazard class. Hydraulic calculation in HASS/Sprink-CALC.

systems.name: Pre-action systems
systems.description: Double-interlocked pre-action systems with UL/FM-listed valves for data halls. Cross-zoned smoke + heat detection for release; electric supervisory air.

systems.name: Dry-pipe sprinklers
systems.description: Dry-pipe systems for unheated areas — loading docks, parking garages — with air-compressor supervisory pressure and rapid-fill on activation.

name: Gas Suppression
short_blurb: Clean-agent gas suppression (NOVEC 1230, FM-200, IG-541) for server rooms, switchgear and equipment-protection applications.
intro_paragraphs: Gas suppression protects equipment where water would cause secondary damage — server rooms, switchgear rooms, museum storage, battery rooms. Clean-agent systems (NOVEC 1230, FM-200, IG-541) discharge a non-conductive, residue-free agent that knocks down fire and dissipates.

Sizing follows NFPA 2001 with leakage compensation per the room's enclosure integrity test (ROOM-INT). Detection is cross-zoned for release; ventilation is interlocked for shut-down; doors are interlocked closed during discharge.
approach_paragraphs: Enclosure integrity is verified by a door-fan pressurisation test (ROOM-INT, NFPA 2001 Annex C). Agent quantity is sized for the actual envelope leakage — not the textbook room volume.

Release logic is cross-zoned (smoke + heat) to prevent false trips. Manual abort and manual release stations are positioned per operator workflow. Discharge testing is performed at commissioning where the spec demands it.

systems.name: NOVEC 1230
systems.description: Hydrofluoroketone clean-agent system for server rooms and high-value electronics. Zero ozone depletion, very low GWP, immediate dissipation post-discharge.

systems.name: FM-200 (HFC-227ea)
systems.description: HFC clean-agent system, established standard for data halls and switchgear protection. Low residue, fast knock-down, NFPA 2001 compliant.

systems.name: Inert gas (IG-541)
systems.description: Inergen / IG-541 inert-gas system for occupied spaces and environmentally-sensitive applications. Zero GWP; design discharge longer than HFC.

name: Detection & Alarm
short_blurb: Smoke detection, heat detection, VESDA aspirating systems and addressable fire alarm panels with PA / voice evacuation.
intro_paragraphs: Fire detection is the first signal that triggers everything else — sprinkler release for pre-action, gas-suppression activation, AHU shutdown, dampers, lift recall and PA evacuation. The detection layer must be sized, located and tested deliberately.

The scope covers spot-type smoke and heat detection, VESDA aspirating smoke detection for data halls and atria, manual call points and addressable fire-alarm panels with PA integration. Detection logic is cross-zoned where the building's actions depend on dual confirmation.
approach_paragraphs: Detector spacing follows NFPA 72 with adjustments for ceiling height, beam pockets and HVAC airflow. Air-sampling systems (VESDA) are designed for very-early-warning in high-value spaces.

Panels are addressable, with point-level fault reporting. Logic for sprinkler release, gas suppression, fan shutdown and lift recall is sequenced in the panel programming and witness-tested at commissioning.

systems.name: Spot detection
systems.description: Photo-electric and ionisation smoke detectors, fixed-temperature and rate-of-rise heat detectors. Spacing per NFPA 72 with ceiling-height and airflow adjustments.

systems.name: VESDA aspirating
systems.description: Air-sampling smoke detection for data halls, atria and high-value storage. Very-early-warning sensitivity with sequenced alert / action / fire levels.

systems.name: Panel & PA integration
systems.description: Addressable fire-alarm panels with full point-level addressing, BMS integration, and PA / voice-evacuation interlock.

name: Smoke Management
short_blurb: Stairwell pressurisation, smoke extraction, atrium smoke control and the dampers that compartmentalise fire spread.
intro_paragraphs: Smoke management keeps egress paths tenable while occupants evacuate. Stairwell pressurisation maintains positive pressure in escape stairs; smoke extraction removes products of combustion from the affected zone; atrium smoke control prevents stratification in tall lobby volumes.
The scope covers fans, dampers, controls and the CFD-backed design that proves the system works under the design fire scenario.
approach_paragraphs: Stairwell pressurisation is designed against the door-opening scenario most adverse — typically all doors closed (max pressure) and one door open (min pressure). Per NFPA 92.

Atrium smoke control uses CFD modelling (Ansys Fluent) where the volume, geometry and stratification matter. Make-up air sources are interlocked to prevent smoke being pushed back into the protected zone.

systems.name: Stairwell pressurisation
systems.description: Fan-and-damper systems maintaining 50 Pa positive pressure in escape stairs. Variable-speed fans with relief dampers to prevent over-pressurisation.

systems.name: Smoke extraction
systems.description: Mechanical smoke extract fans on affected zones, with motorised dampers releasing on alarm. Sized to clear smoke layer above the egress plane.

systems.name: Fire & smoke dampers
systems.description: UL-listed fire dampers and smoke dampers in HVAC ductwork at fire-compartment boundaries. Motorised closure on alarm; fail-safe spring-return.

name: Compliance & NOC
short_blurb: NBC 2016, NFPA 13/72, local fire-authority NOC, Form A — compliance documentation and approval delivered as part of scope.
intro_paragraphs: Fire compliance is the discipline that closes the loop from design through operation. Code review against NBC 2016 (India), NFPA 13/72/2001 (US), or BS 9999/EN 12101 (UK/EU); occupant-load and egress capacity calculations; fire-authority liaison through plan submission, inspection and final NOC.

Compliance is treated as part of scope, not a subcontracted afterthought. The same team that designs the sprinkler system writes the hydraulic-calculation submission and walks the inspector through the witness-test.
approach_paragraphs: Code review happens at scheme stage so the building's egress, compartmentation and suppression strategy is set before architectural drawings freeze. Late code-driven changes are the most expensive kind.

Inspections are scheduled and rehearsed. Common failure modes (missing signage, unsealed penetrations, blocked egress) are caught in a pre-inspection walk so the formal inspection is a confirmation, not a discovery.

systems.name: Code review & submission
systems.description: Compliance review against NBC 2016, state fire prevention rules, local municipal code. Plan submission to the local fire authority with full calculation backup.

systems.name: Witness testing & NOC
systems.description: Hydraulic flow tests, smoke-detection sensitivity tests, gas-suppression discharge tests — all witnessed by the local fire authority and operator's QA team.

systems.name: Documentation handover
systems.description: Full as-built drawings, hydraulic calculations, equipment cut-sheets, maintenance manuals and training records handed over in the operator's required format.

name: Rooftop Solar
short_blurb: Rooftop PV systems for corporate campuses, warehouses, mixed-use developments and industrial estates — net-metered and BMS-monitored.
intro_paragraphs: Rooftop solar is the most accessible renewable generation for commercial and industrial buildings. The scope covers structural assessment of the host roof, mounting design for wind and seismic load, module and inverter selection, string sizing, DC and AC cabling, net-metering hardware, and SCADA monitoring.

Rooftop solar has been delivered as part of the Ingka (IKEA) mixed-use mandate in Noida, integrated with PNG distribution and the wider MEPF scope. Generation is metered, monitored and reported through the building's BMS or a dedicated solar SCADA.
approach_paragraphs: Generation is modelled in PVsyst against site-specific irradiance, tilt, azimuth and shading. Module degradation, temperature derating, and inverter clipping are accounted for in the energy yield estimate.

Structural assessment of the host roof is part of design — not a sign-off at the end. Mounting structures are designed to local wind and seismic load, with anchorage detailed to the as-built roof condition.

systems.name: Module & mounting
systems.description: Mono-PERC or bifacial modules on aluminium / GI mounting structures. Ballasted, penetrating or rail-mount options per host-roof condition.

systems.name: Inverters & strings
systems.description: String inverters for distributed designs, central inverters for high-density rooftops. String sizing to inverter MPPT window with margin for temperature and degradation.

systems.name: Monitoring & metering
systems.description: Net-metering hardware coordinated with the DISCOM, plus inverter-level SCADA monitoring with PR (performance ratio) reporting and alarms.

name: Ground-Mounted Solar
short_blurb: Utility-scale and captive ground-mounted PV plants on fixed-tilt or single-axis tracking structures with HT evacuation.
intro_paragraphs: Ground-mounted solar is where utility-scale generation lives — captive plants for industrial estates, captive-use PPAs for corporate offtake, or simply purpose-built plants for commercial energy supply. The scope is broader: civil foundations, mounting structures, modules, inverters, HT step-up and grid evacuation.

Delivery spans technical due diligence through commissioning and handover to the asset owner's O&M team. Site selection, irradiance modelling, soil testing and grid-connection feasibility are upfront work, not retrofitted to a fixed budget.
approach_paragraphs: Site assessment includes soil bearing capacity (for foundation type), irradiance modelling against multiple TMY datasets, and grid feasibility with the local DISCOM. The energy yield estimate drives the financial model.

Foundation type — concrete pier, ground screw or rammed pile — is chosen against soil condition and project economics. Mounting structures are galvanised steel; modules are mono-PERC with 25-year warranty.

systems.name: Civil & foundations
systems.description: Concrete pier, ground screw or rammed pile foundations for module mounting structures. Drainage, site grading and access roads.

systems.name: Fixed-tilt & tracking
systems.description: Fixed-tilt structures sized to site latitude. Single-axis tracking systems where the additional yield (typically 15-20%) justifies the capex.

systems.name: HT evacuation
systems.description: Inverter step-up via 33 kV / 11 kV transformer, HT switchgear, and evacuation line to the DISCOM's substation. Protection coordinated with grid impedance.

name: Net Metering & Grid Integration
short_blurb: DISCOM-coordinated net metering, gross metering, captive PPAs and the grid-protection layer that ties solar to the utility.
intro_paragraphs: Net metering is the discipline that turns generation into bill credits. Hardware, protection, metering, and the DISCOM application/approval process are all in scope. The same team that engineers the solar plant runs the DISCOM coordination — not a separate consultant.

Grid protection ensures the solar inverter disconnects safely on grid loss (anti-islanding per IEEE 1547 / CEA regulations) and protects both plant and utility from fault current. Hardware selection follows the DISCOM's approved-vendor list.
approach_paragraphs: DISCOM application is filed at design freeze with full single-line diagram, protection coordination report and inverter datasheets. Approval timelines are tracked as critical-path items in the project schedule.

Protection logic is verified by primary injection at commissioning, with anti-islanding tested per the DISCOM's witness protocol. ABT-class meters are sealed and commissioned with the DISCOM inspector present.

systems.name: Net metering hardware
systems.description: Bi-directional ABT-class energy meters per DISCOM specification. Sealed by the DISCOM inspector at commissioning. Trend data accessible via Modbus.

systems.name: Grid protection
systems.description: Anti-islanding protection per IEEE 1547 / CEA, over/under-frequency and voltage protection, ROCOF and vector-shift relays where required.

systems.name: DISCOM coordination
systems.description: Application, approval, hardware compliance verification, and witness testing with the DISCOM. Final approval letter retained in the project handover dossier.

name: Energy Audits
short_blurb: BEE-certified energy audits, ASHRAE Level 1/2/3 audits and retro-commissioning to identify and prove savings opportunities.
intro_paragraphs: Energy audits identify where a building is losing energy and how much it would cost to fix. BEE-certified Type-2 / Type-3 audits are delivered for industrial facilities, alongside ASHRAE Level 1, 2 and 3 audits for commercial buildings.

Findings are quantified with measurement (current loggers, BTU meters, flow meters) — not estimated from nameplate data. ECMs are ranked by simple payback and lifecycle savings, with implementation roadmap and verification plan.
approach_paragraphs: Pre-audit data collection covers 12 months of utility bills, the as-built MEP drawings and the BMS trend store. The on-site survey uses calibrated instruments — power loggers, BTU meters, flow meters, IR thermography.
ECMs are quantified using calibrated energy models (eQuest, TRACE or IES VE) where the savings warrant it. Measurement and verification follows IPMVP Option B or C post-implementation.

systems.name: BEE-certified audits
systems.description: BEE-approved auditors deliver Type-2 / Type-3 audits for industrial mandates. PAT cycle reporting and SEC tracking.

systems.name: ASHRAE Level 1/2/3
systems.description: Walk-through to investment-grade audits per ASHRAE 211. Level depends on the operator's depth of decision-making.

systems.name: M&V (post-implementation)
systems.description: Measurement and verification per IPMVP Options A / B / C / D to confirm savings against baseline. Trend data analysed quarterly.

name: LEED / IGBC Compliance
short_blurb: Green-building certification — LEED, IGBC and GRIHA — from design intent through documentation and final award.
intro_paragraphs: Green-building certification rewards measured performance — energy efficiency, water conservation, indoor air quality, materials sourcing. The engineering and documentation that earn LEED, IGBC and GRIHA credits are delivered from design through final award.
The Common Central Secretariat (IGBC Gold) and Nalanda University (net-zero) show what's achievable when sustainability is baked into the engineering from concept — not retrofitted at handover.
approach_paragraphs: Credit targeting happens at scheme stage with the architect and operator. ASHRAE 90.1 baseline modelling, water-use reduction calculations, and material EPDs are all sequenced into the design programme so credits are evidence-backed, not aspirational.
Documentation hand-over is dossier-ready for the rating-body review. Pre-submission audit catches gaps before formal submission.

systems.name: LEED
systems.description: USGBC LEED v4 / v4.1 certification — Energy & Atmosphere, Water Efficiency, Indoor Air Quality, Materials & Resources credit categories.

systems.name: IGBC
systems.description: Indian Green Building Council certification under New Construction, Existing Building or Factory Buildings rating systems. Local Indian-context calibration.

systems.name: GRIHA
systems.description: TERI's GRIHA rating for buildings in the Indian climate — five-star scale based on energy, water, materials and indoor environmental quality.

name: DDC & Field Controls
short_blurb: Distributed Direct Digital Control panels and field devices for HVAC, plumbing, electrical and fire-system integration.
intro_paragraphs: DDC is the field-level intelligence that turns mechanical and electrical equipment into a controllable, observable system. DDC panels run BTL-certified controllers with point-level addressing, vendor-neutral protocols (BACnet, Modbus) and BMS-tied trend logging from day one.

Sensor and actuator selection is part of design — not delegated to an installer. Pressure sensors, temperature probes, control valves and damper actuators are specified for the application's response time, accuracy and BMS protocol.
approach_paragraphs: Point lists are signed off pre-commissioning with the operator's facility team. Tag dictionaries follow a published convention so downstream DCIM or CMMS integration is painless.
Control sequences are written in IEC 61131 Structured Text or vendor-equivalent graphical logic. Sequences are commissioned with witness sign-off — not assumed working after panel power-up.

systems.name: BACnet DDC panels
systems.description: BTL-certified DDC controllers with BACnet/IP and MS/TP communication. Point counts sized for HVAC, plumbing and electrical integration with 20% spare capacity.

systems.name: Field sensors & actuators
systems.description: Temperature, humidity, pressure, flow and energy sensors with the right response time and accuracy. Control valves, damper actuators and VSDs specified per application.

systems.name: Control sequences
systems.description: Sequences for chilled-water plant staging, AHU setpoint reset, demand-controlled ventilation, lighting and energy management. Commissioned with witness sign-off.

name: SCADA & Head-End
short_blurb: BMS head-end servers, SCADA dashboards, historian and the alarm hierarchy that turns DDC into operator-actionable intelligence.
intro_paragraphs: The SCADA head-end is where DDC data becomes operator intelligence. Redundant head-end servers, real-time dashboards, a historian with multi-year trend retention, and alarm hierarchies pre-agreed with the facility team are delivered together.

Reports are scheduled to land in the operator's inbox without further intervention. Trend retention follows the operator's analytics or compliance need — typically 3 years for energy, 7 years for regulated environments.
approach_paragraphs: Dashboards are designed against the operator's workflow — operator console, supervisor view, executive summary. Each layer surfaces only what's actionable at that role.
Alarms are categorised (operator / supervisor / critical) with escalation rules. False-alarm tuning happens in the first 30 days of operation, not deferred.

systems.name: Head-end servers
systems.description: Redundant BMS head-end servers (active-passive or active-active) hosted on the operator's infrastructure or as a managed service.

systems.name: Dashboards & historian
systems.description: Role-based dashboards with historian for trend logging and analysis. Multi-year retention per operator's compliance need.

systems.name: Alarm management
systems.description: Categorised alarms with escalation rules, suppression for known maintenance events, and analytics for nuisance-alarm tuning.

name: Fire Alarm & PA
short_blurb: Addressable fire-alarm panels with PA / voice-evacuation integration, lift recall logic and BMS interlocks.
intro_paragraphs: Fire-alarm and PA integration sits at the intersection of life-safety code and operator usability. Addressable panels are delivered with full point-level addressing, EN 54 / UL 864 compliance, and PA / voice-evacuation integration that provides clear pre-recorded messaging during evacuation.
Interlock logic with the BMS sequences AHU shutdown, smoke damper actuation and lift recall on alarm — verified by witness testing at commissioning.
approach_paragraphs: Panel architecture follows EN 54 with point-level addressing. Detection logic for sprinkler release, gas-suppression discharge and PA evacuation is sequenced in panel programming, not in a separate controller.
Voice messages are pre-recorded with the operator's preferred language and tone. Manual call points are interlocked for tier-1 release where the building's evacuation plan demands it.

name: CCTV & Access Control
short_blurb: IP CCTV, access-control panels, biometric and card-reader integration with VMS and the building's identity-management system.
intro_paragraphs: Security systems sit alongside fire and BMS as a third controls layer. The scope covers IP CCTV (cameras, NVR/VMS, analytics), access-control panels (card readers, biometric, controller), and the integration that lets a single operator workflow span all three.
VMS is selected against the operator's preferred platform (Genetec, Milestone, Avigilon, Bosch). Cameras are picked for the scene — wide-angle for atria, narrow for entries, low-light for car parks.
approach_paragraphs: Camera coverage is planned in iVMS or equivalent against the operator's surveillance objectives. Storage is sized to the retention window and per-camera frame rate.

Access control follows the operator's identity policy — card, biometric, or both. Anti-passback, mantrap and tailgating-prevention logic is configured for sensitive zones (data halls, treasury, equipment rooms).

systems.name: IP CCTV
systems.description: IP cameras (fixed dome, PTZ, multi-sensor) on Cat-6A PoE distribution with NVR or VMS recording. Edge analytics for motion, line-cross and people-count.

systems.name: Access control
systems.description: Card-reader and biometric access-control with controller panels, electric strikes, magnetic locks and request-to-exit sensors.

name: Energy Management
short_blurb: Sub-metering, energy dashboards, demand-response logic and the analytics that prove operational efficiency.
intro_paragraphs: Energy management turns sub-meter data into operational decisions. Granular sub-metering is delivered across HVAC, lighting, IT, plug and process loads, with dashboards that show consumption by zone, sub-system and time-of-day.

Analytics overlay benchmarks against ASHRAE 90.1 or operator-specific KPIs (EUI, PUE, kWh per occupant, kWh per m²). Demand-response logic shifts loads off-peak where the utility tariff makes it worthwhile.
approach_paragraphs: Sub-metering granularity follows what the operator can act on — feeder-level for buildings, branch-level for premium tenants, per-equipment for energy-intensive zones.
Dashboards are designed for two audiences — facility operator (daily) and sustainability lead (monthly). Each gets the visualisation that drives their decision.

systems.name: Sub-metering
systems.description: Class-1 sub-meters at feeder, branch and per-equipment level. Communications via Modbus / BACnet into the BMS for trend logging.

systems.name: Energy dashboards
systems.description: Real-time and historical dashboards showing consumption by zone, sub-system and time-of-day. Benchmarked against operator KPIs.

systems.name: Demand response & DR

name: DCIM Integration
short_blurb: Data Centre Infrastructure Management integration with open feeds (Modbus, BACnet, SNMP) into the operator's chosen DCIM platform.
intro_paragraphs: Data centre operators run on DCIM — the platform that consolidates power, cooling, space and IT into one operational view. The integration layer feeding BMS, EPMS, fire and security data into the operator's DCIM via open feeds (Modbus, BACnet, SNMP) is delivered as standard scope.
The objective is portability. Standardised tag dictionaries, documented point lists, and joint witness-tests on integration mean the operator inherits a working system — not a vendor lock-in.
approach_paragraphs: Tag dictionaries are signed off pre-commissioning with the operator's DCIM team. Point lists are documented in the format required by the chosen DCIM (Sunbird, Schneider EcoStruxure, Vertiv Trellis).
Witness tests on the BMS-DCIM hand-off prove every tag is mapped, scaled and timestamped correctly. Edge cases — comms loss, partial reads, stale data — are tested before sign-off.

systems.name: Open-protocol feeds
