name: 24/7 Facility Management
short_blurb: Round-the-clock operations management for HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire and BMS — single accountable team, single SLA.
intro_paragraphs: Round-the-clock facility management means every MEP system has a qualified operator on duty, every event is logged, and every escalation follows a defined path. O&M contracts span every discipline Unique Engineers installs — a single accountable team, a single performance SLA.

Coverage is structured by shift, with handover briefings, log-book entries, and exception-reporting into the operator's CAFM. Routine rounds verify equipment status; reactive response handles tickets in priority order.
approach_paragraphs: Shift structure follows the operator's coverage need — typically 8/8/8 or 12/12 with weekend coverage. Senior engineers cover the morning shift; experienced technicians cover nights.
Daily handover briefings transfer open tickets, equipment status and overnight incidents. Weekly operations reviews trend KPIs (energy, downtime, ticket-close rate) with the operator.

systems.name: Shift operations
systems.description: Multi-shift cover with senior engineer on morning, experienced technicians on nights. Handover briefings, log-book and CAFM updates every shift.

systems.name: Routine rounds
systems.description: Scheduled rounds verifying equipment status, plant-room conditions, sensor readings against expected ranges. Anomalies logged and ticketed.

systems.name: Reactive ticketing
systems.description: Priority-based ticket queue (P1–P4) with defined response and resolution SLAs. CAFM-tracked with closure verification.

name: Preventive Maintenance
short_blurb: OEM-aligned PM schedules loaded into CMMS from the project hand-over dossier — operational on day one of the O&M contract.
intro_paragraphs: Preventive maintenance is the discipline of doing the work before the failure happens. PM schedules are loaded into the CMMS with full asset hierarchy, OEM-specified PM frequencies, spares lists and skill requirements — so the programme is operational from day one of the contract.
Where the MEP system was installed by the same team, the hand-over dossier seeds the PM plan. The asset register comes with manufacturer datasheets, warranties and spares lists already attached.
approach_paragraphs: Schedules are loaded into CMMS (Maximo, eAM, MaintainX or operator-preferred) with full asset tagging, location hierarchy and OEM-spec frequencies. Annual schedule review tunes frequencies against actual equipment behaviour.
PM completion is tracked against compliance percentage. Skipped or overdue PMs are escalated. Spares are pre-positioned for high-frequency items.

systems.name: CMMS-loaded schedules
systems.description: PM schedules loaded with full asset tagging, OEM frequencies, work-order templates and spares lists. Operational day-one of the contract.

systems.name: Skill-matched execution
systems.description: PMs assigned to technicians by skill match. Critical PMs (chiller overhaul, transformer testing) executed by senior specialists, not generalist staff.

systems.name: Compliance reporting
systems.description: PM compliance % tracked monthly, with overdue escalation, root-cause review and corrective action. KPI feeds operator's monthly ops review.

name: Predictive Maintenance
short_blurb: BMS-trend analytics, vibration monitoring, IR thermography and harmonic analysis to spot drift before it becomes failure.
intro_paragraphs: Predictive maintenance overlays the BMS trend store with analytics to spot drift before it becomes failure. Chiller approach temperatures, motor vibration where instrumented, harmonic distortion on critical feeders, refrigerant superheat — all signals that something is wrong before the alarm sounds.
Diagnostics include vibration spectrum analysis on rotating equipment, IR thermography on switchgear and motor terminations, and refrigerant-cycle analysis on chillers.
approach_paragraphs: Trend baselines are established in the first 30 days of operation. Drift thresholds are set per equipment class with operator sign-off.
Quarterly diagnostic surveys cover IR thermography, vibration sampling and refrigerant-cycle review. Findings are scheduled into the PM workorder pipeline.

systems.name: Trend analytics
systems.description: BMS historian data analysed for approach temperatures, fan/pump curve drift, valve authority degradation and other early-warning signals.

systems.name: IR thermography
systems.description: Quarterly thermal imaging of switchgear, motor terminations, cable trays and bus trunking — identifies loose connections and asymmetric loading.

systems.name: Vibration & refrigerant
systems.description: Vibration spectrum sampling on rotating equipment, refrigerant superheat/subcooling logging on chillers — both feed equipment-specific health scores.

name: Asset Lifecycle Management
short_blurb: Asset condition tracking, capex planning, replacement scheduling and end-of-life decommissioning over the full asset life.
intro_paragraphs: Asset lifecycle management turns capital equipment into a planned, financially-tracked portfolio. Condition, residual life, performance degradation and energy efficiency are tracked over the full asset life — surfacing capex needs years before they bite the operator's budget.

End-of-life decommissioning and replacement is staged into the operator's capex planning cycle, with the new equipment specified for current load profile, regulatory framework and energy-efficiency target — not just like-for-like replaced.
approach_paragraphs: Asset register is tagged with original install date, expected life, residual-life estimate based on condition monitoring, and replacement budget. Reviewed annually with the operator's finance team.
Replacement planning identifies opportunities — not just obligations. Energy-efficiency upgrade, capacity rightsizing and digital-twin readiness are evaluated at every major replacement.

systems.name: Asset register & condition
systems.description: Full asset register with install date, expected life, residual-life estimate, condition score and replacement budget. Updated quarterly.

systems.name: Capex planning
systems.description: 5-year rolling capex plan aligned with operator's finance cycle. Replacement timing, vendor selection and TCO trade-offs documented.

systems.name: Decommissioning
systems.description: End-of-life decommissioning with refrigerant recovery, asbestos surveys where relevant, and material recycling per IGBC waste-stream guidelines.

name: Rapid Response Teams
short_blurb: Pre-positioned rapid-response teams with critical spares for the top-quartile-impact failure modes — keeping MTTR inside SLA.
intro_paragraphs: Rapid response is the discipline of restoring service quickly when the failure happens anyway. Teams are pre-positioned near major client sites, with critical spares for the top-quartile failure modes — chiller compressors, UPS batteries, breaker mechanisms, BMS controllers.
MTTR (mean-time-to-repair) is tracked per failure class. The objective is unambiguous: keep the worst-case incident inside the SLA window, every time.
approach_paragraphs: Failure-mode analysis identifies the top 20% of failures by frequency × downtime impact. Spares for those are pre-positioned; technicians for those are pre-trained.
Response is rehearsed. Tabletop exercises and live drills cover the worst-case scenarios — chiller failure on the design-day, UPS battery cascade, fire-pump start-up failure.

systems.name: Pre-positioned spares

systems.name: Trained response teams
systems.description: Technicians pre-trained on the equipment installed at each site. Senior specialists on call for tier-1 incidents.

systems.description: Tabletop exercises quarterly, live drills annually. Worst-case scenarios — chiller failure, UPS cascade, fire-pump start failure — practised end-to-end.
